items.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I did have the privilege and chance to meet Papa Jo... he’s wonderful as a friend.

ctx.x: Can you quickly name a couple of the major influences on you, the drummers you listened to on the way up?

Oh, wow, there’s so many I listened to and still listen to. Well there’s naturally there’s Sonny Greer with Duke Ellington’s band. I used to, you know, always glued my ear to, and there was the wonderful, great Jo Jones, Papa Jo you know, and he was just wonderful not only as a drummer but he’s wonderful as a friend. He’s just a wonderful guy. Naturally there’s Max Roach I always, always listened to him when I get a chance to listen to Max or go see him. Roy Haynes. Roy Haynes is another master drummer. So…
What do you feel about the way jazz is going right now? The future of it, and as someone who’s making their living in jazz, does it bode well do you think?
